issues.item: Story Feels Unreal: The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, these items are hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile. 'Story Feels Unreal' and especially 'Overwhelm on Recall' imply a disjointed, emotionally intense trauma memory, which fits the strong Memory↔Threat links. In contrast, 'Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily' suggests unusually easy narrative access to the trauma and directly pulls against the other memory items. For a severe PTSD profile centered on intrusive, overwhelming childhood domestic violence memories, this Memory combination is clinically inconsistent.

issues.item: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, these two items directly contradict each other: being able to talk about the trauma very easily is incompatible with simultaneously being unable to put the event into words. This is a clear within-node inconsistency.

vignette: Sara is a 30-year-old Middle Eastern woman who works as a bartender at a local bar in her neighborhood. She has been divorced for several years and currently lives alone. Growing up, Sara witnessed domestic violence between her parents, which has left deep emotional scars that persist into adulthood. The traumatic event she experienced during childhood was particularly potent because it involved repeated scenes of violence where sudden movements and aggressive actions by her father would escalate into physical confrontations with her mother. These episodes were both frightening and confusing for young Sara, who had to witness the violent outbursts while also trying to protect herself from the ensuing chaos. Over time, these memories have become deeply ingrained in Sara’s psyche, leading to an intense sense of vulnerability and a need to constantly monitor potential threats. When she recalls those traumatic moments now, they are overwhelming and difficult to verbalize. She often feels unable to put into words what happened, which only intensifies her distress. Sara’s negative appraisals about herself and others have been shaped by these memories. She has come to believe that she can't rely on herself in times of crisis; this self-doubt exacerbates the overwhelming emotions when she thinks about those violent episodes. As a result, Sara constantly feels threatened and is always looking for signs of danger around her. This constant vigilance stems from the belief that people cannot be trusted, which makes it hard for her to feel safe in most environments. Her fear of sudden movements by others puts her on guard at all times, as she associates these with the violent actions witnessed during childhood. For instance, while working as a bartender, Sara is particularly anxious when patrons are loud or make quick gestures. The same level of anxiety extends to other open spaces where she feels exposed and vulnerable. To cope with this overwhelming sense of threat and memory intrusion, Sara has developed several maladaptive strategies. She mentally rehearses worst-case scenarios in her mind, believing that being prepared will help protect her from potential harm. This rehearsal often leads to a spiral where the memories become more vivid and intrusive, further reinforcing her negative appraisals about herself and others. Sara’s efforts to control her emotions only intensify when she remembers the violent scenes of her childhood. These attempts to suppress her feelings make it even harder for her to process what happened, leading her to feel increasingly isolated and mistrustful. She repeatedly checks doors and windows at home, ensuring they are locked securely, as if these actions can somehow shield her from potential threats. The loop of negative appraisals, heightened threat perception, overwhelming memories, and maladaptive coping strategies has tightened over time. Sara’s attempts to control her environment through avoidance and rehearsal only exacerbate the very issues she is trying to manage. For example, her fear of open spaces makes it difficult for her to socialize or even leave her home often. What finally brought Sara to seek help was a recent incident at work where a customer’s sudden movement triggered a panic attack. She realized that these episodes were becoming more frequent and impacting her ability to function both professionally and personally. Sara is most afraid of losing control entirely, but she also hopes for a way to process her memories without feeling overwhelmed by them. Sara’s journey towards healing requires addressing the core beliefs about herself and others while finding healthier ways to manage her fears and memories. She hopes that with professional help, she can regain some sense of security and trust in herself and those around her.
